what.text: Doxycycline is a tetracycline-class antibiotic, taken by mouth. Its labels list infections it treats or prevents, including anthrax after exposure and malaria prevention in short-term travellers.
For acne, the standard doxycycline label says: "In severe acne, doxycycline may be useful adjunctive therapy." That means an add-on to other acne treatment, not a stand-alone acne approval.

Oracea is a separate, lower-strength 40 mg capsule approved only for the inflamed bumps of rosacea. Its label says it is not bioequivalent to other doxycycline products and must not be used to treat infections.

Adonis carries doxycycline hyclate 100 mg capsules, taken by mouth (30-day and 90-day supplies). Doxycycline hyclate 100 mg capsules are sold in the US as FDA-approved generic products, for example under ANDA 062396.

research.text: The rosacea evidence FDA reviewed is two 16-week randomized trials of Oracea in 537 people. For acne, the standard label relies on its adjunctive-therapy wording rather than describing acne trials. Two published acne trials are listed below.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Oracea 40 mg in rosacea: two trials (FDA label)

facts.v: 2 multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials
537 adults with rosacea (10 to 40 papules and pustules, two or fewer nodules); 269 on Oracea
change in inflamed lesion count, and the share rated clear or almost clear

research.found: Lesion counts fell by 11.8 vs 5.9 (study 1) and 9.5 vs 4.3 (study 2) on Oracea vs placebo. 30.7% vs 19.4%, and 14.8% vs 6.3%, were rated clear or almost clear. Redness did not improve significantly compared with placebo.

research.title: Low-dose doxycycline in moderate acne (Skidmore et al.)

facts.v: multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, two university clinics
51 adults with moderate facial acne; 40 completed
doxycycline hyclate 20 mg tablets (Periostat) twice daily, or placebo
lesion counts, clinician's global assessment, skin bacteria and antibiotic resistance

research.found: The doxycycline group had a larger percentage fall in blackheads and whiteheads and in inflamed lesions than the placebo group. No change in skin bacteria or antibiotic resistance was detected.

research.title: Doxycycline vs spironolactone in adult women with acne (FASCE)

facts.v: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel groups; both arms also used benzoyl peroxide
doxycycline for 3 months then placebo for 3 months, vs spironolactone for 6 months
treatment success on the AFAST acne score at months 4 and 6

research.found: Success at 6 months was significantly higher with spironolactone than with doxycycline (P = 0.007). The trial enrolled women only.

us.text: Doxycycline is an FDA-approved prescription antibiotic. Vibramycin capsules were approved in 1967 and generic doxycycline hyclate capsules followed. Oracea 40 mg was approved in 2006 for rosacea bumps. Its acne use on the standard label is as adjunctive (add-on) therapy for severe acne. As of October 31, 2026.

side.text: The FDA labels warn of permanent tooth discoloration when taken during tooth development, sun sensitivity, irritation and ulcers of the esophagus, raised pressure around the brain, severe skin reactions and C. difficile diarrhea.

items.text: use during tooth development (the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to age 8) may permanently discolor the teeth yellow-gray-brown. Enamel defects have been reported. Superficial discoloration of adult permanent teeth, reversible with stopping and professional cleaning, has also been reported.
an exaggerated sunburn reaction has been seen in some people taking tetracyclines. The label says to stop at the first sign of skin redness.
rare esophagitis and esophageal ulcers have been reported with capsules and tablets, mostly in people who took them just before going to bed. The label advises taking them with plenty of fluid.

intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) can cause headache, blurred vision and vision loss, which may be permanent. The risk is higher in overweight women of childbearing age. Use with isotretinoin should be avoided.
including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis and DRESS have been reported.
C. difficile diarrhea, from mild to fatal colitis, has been reported with nearly all antibiotics, including doxycycline.
Oracea's patient information says it can darken the skin, scars, teeth, gums, nails and whites of the eyes.
more common than placebo were nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, high blood pressure, sinusitis and raised liver enzyme (AST), among others.
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, rare liver injury, and allergic reactions including anaphylaxis.
Oracea's label says to avoid it in the second and third trimesters and not to breastfeed during treatment and for 5 days after.

surprises: Doxycycline is commonly described as an approved acne treatment, but the standard FDA label says only that "in severe acne, doxycycline may be useful adjunctive therapy"; it is an add-on, for severe acne.
Oracea, the doxycycline approved for rosacea, showed no significant effect on rosacea redness in its trials, and its label says it must not be used to treat infections.
Tooth staining is usually linked only to children, but the label also reports superficial discoloration of adult permanent teeth.
